title: Selecting the Starting Value From Valuation Reports on a Total Loss
content:
**Rule.** Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), the starting value of the vehicle value paid to a loss payee is chosen from the valuation reports. These are the estimate entries of the claim, each with the actual cash value it records.
- **Two reports close together.** When the two entries with the highest estimate sequences differ by no more than the report spread limit of 0.10 (10 percent) of the lower of the two, the starting value is their average.
- **Two reports far apart.** When they differ by more than that, it is the lower of the two.
- **Fewer than two reports.** When the claim has fewer than two such entries, it is the actual cash value on the total loss declaration.

### Input, judgement, output (hypothetical reports)

| Two highest-sequence reports (USD) | Spread compared with 10 percent of the lower | Starting value (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| 8,400.00 and 8,950.00 | 550.00 against 840.00: within | 8,675.00 (average) |
| 9,000.00 and 9,900.00 | 900.00 against 900.00: no more than the limit | 9,450.00 (average) |
| 8,000.00 and 9,100.00 | 1,100.00 against 800.00: more than the limit | 8,000.00 (lower) |
| Only one report on the claim | Not applicable | Actual cash value on the total loss declaration |

When a claim has three estimate entries, only the two with the highest estimate sequences are compared.
